```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r include=FALSE}
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
davisdata <- read.csv(file="UCDavis.csv")
```
 Our Goal is to answer this question Is there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row
 you choose to sit in??

# Introduction  
The question is this: Is there a relationship between where you sit in class and how much you drink?   
Data is from UCDavis Math116 class    

$H_0$ There is no relationship between what row in class you sit in and how much you drink.   
$H_A$ There is a difference between what row in clas you sit in and how much you drink.  



# Methods 
Seat is categorical  
Alcohol is numerical  

# Data Summaries


## Now add in boxplot

```{r}
boxplot(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```

Graph demonstrates that if the student sits in the back they are more likely to consume more ounces per week of alcohol than the students who sits in the front or middle.  

## Numerical Summaries  

```{r}
favstats(alcohol~Seat,data=ucdavis1)
```

The numerical summary shows that the students who sit in the back drink about ten more ounches of alcohol than the students who sit in the middle and front seats. Students who sit in the middle or back drink about 2 to 3 ounches of alcohol per week. 


## Inferential Tests

```{r}
model1 <- aov(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
summary.aov(model1)
```
The P value is 0.000116, which is less than 0.05, so we fail to reject the $H_0$ and conclude that there is a relationship between where someone sits and how much they drink.

```{r}
plot(TukeyHSD(model1))
```

The tukey graph shows that there is a difference in alcohol consumption between students who sit in the front, middle, and back.There is no difference in alcohol consumption between the front and middle row.
